The page's most transferable content is the COUNTER-INTUITIVE FLUID ADVICE IN ACUTE COLIC and the list of DRUGS THAT CAUSE OR WORSEN STONES. eTG CROSS-CHECK 2026-09-24: every licensed-source dose compared with Therapeutic Guidelines (paraphrased, no eTG text stored); results and additions in the page's eTG cross-check section.

claims.claim: KIDNEY STONES ARE COMMON and RENAL COLIC DUE TO MOVEMENT OF A STONE INTO THE URETER IS THE MOST COMMON SYMPTOM. ⚠️ 70-80% CONSIST OF CALCIUM OXALATE AND/OR CALCIUM PHOSPHATE, WITH 5-10% CONTAINING URIC ACID
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ACUTE RENAL COLIC: ⚠️ UNLESS CONTRAINDICATED, USE AN NSAID (ANY ROUTE) FIRST-LINE TO RELIEVE PAIN. ⚠️ OPIOIDS CAUSE HIGH RATES OF VOMITING AND MAY BE CONSIDERED ONLY IF NSAIDs ARE INADEQUATE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ THE COUNTER-INTUITIVE POINT: IN ACUTE RENAL COLIC, NORMAL FLUID INTAKE IS RECOMMENDED. INCREASING URINE OUTPUT THROUGH HIGH FLUID INTAKE IS LIKELY TO INCREASE THE RISK OF OBSTRUCTION AND WORSEN PAIN
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: SELECTIVE ALPHA-BLOCKERS are sometimes used in SELECTED PATIENTS WITH LOWER URETERAL STONES UNDER 10 mm to help stone passage -- ⚠️ ONLY PATIENTS WITH STONES 5-10 mm IN SIZE ARE LIKELY TO BENEFIT, DUE TO THE HIGH SPONTANEOUS PASSAGE RATE OF UP TO 89% FOR SMALLER STONES. SURGERY MAY BE REQUIRED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: PREVENTION: ⚠️ THE RECURRENCE RATE IS HIGH. INCREASING FLUID INTAKE -- TO ACHIEVE A URINE OUTPUT ABOVE 2 L DAILY IF POSSIBLE -- IS IMPORTANT IN PREVENTION. Dietary measures such as RESTRICTING SALT INTAKE may also help, and ⚠️ NORMAL DIETARY CALCIUM INTAKE IS RECOMMENDED -- NOT RESTRICTED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ THE FLUID ADVICE IS OPPOSITE IN THE TWO SETTINGS: NORMAL FLUID INTAKE DURING ACUTE COLIC, BUT INCREASED FLUID INTAKE FOR PREVENTION. WHEN FLUID AND DIETARY MEASURES ARE INEFFECTIVE, CONSIDER DRUG TREATMENT to prevent new stones or growth of existing stones -- SEEK SPECIALIST ADVICE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: PREVENTIVE DRUGS: ALLOPURINOL decreases urinary urate and is used for URIC ACID OR CALCIUM OXALATE STONES IN PEOPLE WITH HYPERURICOSURIA. POTASSIUM CITRATE increases urine pH and citrate concentration and inhibits crystal formation -- used for URIC ACID OR CALCIUM OXALATE STONES, ESPECIALLY IN PEOPLE WITH HYPOCITRATURIA. THIAZIDE DIURETICS reduce calcium excretion -- used for CALCIUM STONES IN PEOPLE WITH HYPERCALCIURIA
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ DRUGS THAT AFFECT STONE RISK: WHETHER ASCORBIC ACID INCREASES THE RISK OF CALCIUM OXALATE STONE FORMATION IS UNCLEAR, BUT DOSES ABOVE 1 g DAILY SHOULD BE AVOIDED. The effect of CALCIUM AND/OR VITAMIN D SUPPLEMENTATION on recurrence IS UNCLEAR -- use with caution, and ADVISE THAT CALCIUM SUPPLEMENTS ARE TAKEN WITH FOOD TO BIND OXALATE AND DECREASE URINARY OXALATE EXCRETION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ CARBONIC ANHYDRASE INHIBITORS -- eg ACETAZOLAMIDE, TOPIRAMATE -- CAN INCREASE THE RISK OF CALCIUM PHOSPHATE STONES. PROBENECID CAN INCREASE THE RISK OF URIC ACID STONES. ⚠️ RENALLY EXCRETED DRUGS WITH LOW SOLUBILITY AT URINE pH, eg CIPROFLOXACIN, MAY CRYSTALLISE IN THE URINARY TRACT FORMING STONES, ESPECIALLY AT HIGH DOSES
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Kidney stones' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/genitourinary-drugs/other-drugs-urinary-tract-disorders/kidney-stones, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Recurrent calcium stones with persistent hypercalciuria (specialist advice): chlortalidone 12.5 mg orally daily up to 50 mg, or hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily up to 50 mg twice daily, or indapamide 2.5 mg daily (all off-label); avoid in gout.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Kidney and Urinary guideline: 'Kidney and ureteric stones in adults' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Kidney%20and%20Urinary&topicfile=kidney-overview&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_KUG_Kidney-and-ureteric-stones-in-adults_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Measures to prevent calcium-based kidney and ureteric stones'

claims.claim: Hypocitraturia or uric acid/cystine stones: potassium citrate usually 4 to 8 g daily, titrated to urine pH and citrate (target pH 6-7 for uric acid, at least 7.5 for cystine); cystinuria also needs at least 3 L fluid daily.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Kidney and Urinary guideline: 'Kidney and ureteric stones in adults' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Kidney%20and%20Urinary&topicfile=kidney-overview&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_KUG_Kidney-and-ureteric-stones-in-adults_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Stone-specific measures to prevent kidney and ureteric stones'

claims.claim: Urgent ED transfer for fever, UTI, severe pain, pregnancy or single kidney; refer to urology if stone over 6 mm, eGFR 60 or less, colic over 2 weeks, or not passed by 4 weeks; UTI with obstruction needs urgent decompression.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Kidney and Urinary guideline: 'Kidney and ureteric stones in adults' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Kidney%20and%20Urinary&topicfile=kidney-overview&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_KUG_Kidney-and-ureteric-stones-in-adults_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Indications for emergency management or specialist referral of adults with kidney and ureteric stones'

claims.claim: Offer metabolic evaluation (24-hour urine, stone analysis, bloods) for recurrent, bilateral, non-calcium or single-kidney stones, family history, age under 18 or high-risk occupations.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Kidney and Urinary guideline: 'Kidney and ureteric stones in adults' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Kidney%20and%20Urinary&topicfile=kidney-overview&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_KUG_Kidney-and-ureteric-stones-in-adults_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Metabolic evaluation of kidney and ureteric stones in adults'
